Modified the MRP slightly so that it instead calls `print("[PID %d - %d] Test" % [OS.get_process_id(), Time.get_ticks_msec()])` on timeout to provide a bit more detail. I then ran the MRP for a little bit on 4.7.stable (more than enough for all the 1s timers to fire), but only got output from 4 of them (PIDs: 14899, 14900, 14901, 14905). This seems to confirm this behaviour, which is not what I would expect.

I just put together a custom build of Godot 4.7.1 using code from the PR linked here (https://github.com/Godot-Lyon/godot/pull/2) and revisited this MRP using the print statement modification mentioned here (https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/120678#issuecomment-4819092432). It appears that this effectively fixes the issue for me, although I have noticed that it launches the first 8 instances first, then the other 8 about a second later. IIRC if something were to go wrong, then only the first 8 instances will have its output recorded, although this was more of a occasional thing testing this with another project. `Godot v4.7.1.stable unknown -
